```{r mod_make1}
# ─── 16. First Regression (Backward Selection) ───────────────────────────────────────

# Ensure all variables used for the model exist in the data frame
# The lm() function is used to fit linear models
# Here, LN_SPPSF is the dependent variable, the others are factors / predictors
# data is the data frame containing the variables to be used in the model

mod_one <- lm(LN_SPPSF ~ ARTERIAL + QABOVE_AVG + QBELOW_AVG_POOR +
                SINGLE_FAMILY1STORY + SINGLE_FAMILY2STORY + HALF_DUPLEX1STORY +
                HALF_DUPLEX2STORY + TWO_PLUS_BATHS + POWDER_ROOM + SMALL + LARGE +
                SMALLEST + LARGEST + YB_PRE_1929 + YB_1946_TO_1960 + YB_POST_1961 +
                LN_GARAGESPACES + FIREPLACE + HOT_WATER + ELEC_BASEBOARD + WALL +
                CENTRAL_AIR + GOOD + FAIR + POOR + VERY_POOR_UNSOUND +
                MONTHS_6TO22 + MONTHS_23TO30 + CRAWL + SLAB,
               data = data)

# scope = list allows for forcibly including parameters in the final model
# Omitting (line 303 below) allows the tuning to exclude any parameter it chooses
# Use trace = 1 for verbose, 0 for no output
step_mod_one <- stats::step(mod_one, direction = 'backward',
                            scope = list(lower = ~ MONTHS_6TO22 + MONTHS_23TO30,
                                         upper = formula(mod_one)), trace = 0)
```

## Custom Functions

```{r functions}
wrap_kable <- function(labels, names, n = 10, caption = NULL){
  # labels:   character vector of cell‐labels
  # names:    names(labels) to use as colnames
  # n:        max number of cols per line
  # caption:  base caption (we’ll append the chunk range)
  
  total <- length(labels)
  idxs  <- split(seq_len(total), ceiling(seq_len(total)/n))
  # print(caption)
  
  for(i in seq_along(idxs)){
    ii   <- idxs[[i]]
    mat  <- matrix(labels[ii], nrow = 1,
                   dimnames = list(NULL, names[ii]))
    cap  <- if(is.null(caption)) "" 
            else paste0(caption, " (cols ", min(ii), "–", max(ii), ")")
    print(kable(mat, caption = cap))
  }
}
```

            'SINGLE_FAMILY2STORY','HALF_DUPLEX1STORY','HALF_DUPLEX2STORY','TWO_PLUS_BATHS',
            'POWDER_ROOM','SMALL','LARGE','SMALLEST','LARGEST','QABOVE_AVG','QBELOW_AVG_POOR',
            'LN_GARAGESPACES','YB_PRE_1929', 'YB_1930_TO_1945', 'YB_1946_TO_1960','YB_POST_1961','FIREPLACE',
            'HOT_WATER','ELEC_BASEBOARD','WALL','CENTRAL_AIR','CRAWL','SLAB','GOOD','FAIR','POOR',
            'VERY_POOR_UNSOUND','MONTHS_1TO9','MONTHS_10TO16', 'MONTHS_17TO24')

full_var_form <- reformulate(predictors, response = "LN_PRICE")
mod_two_rev  <- lm(full_var_form, data = df)

current_mod <- mod_two_rev
current_preds <- predictors

repeat {
  ss <- summary(current_mod)
  pvals <- ss$coefficients[-1, 4]    # drop intercept
  worst_p <- max(pvals, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  if (worst_p <= 0.10) break          # stop when everyone’s in
  remove_var <- names(pvals)[which.max(pvals)]
  
  message("Dropping ", remove_var, " (p=", signif(worst_p,2), ")")
  current_preds <- setdiff(current_preds, remove_var)
  current_mod   <- update(current_mod, reformulate(current_preds, "LN_PRICE"))
}

final_mod <- current_mod

# 4.1 Coefficients & p-values
coef(final_mod)
# or for full table:
summary(final_mod)$coefficients

# 4.2 R², F-statistic & ANOVA
summary(final_mod)$r.squared
summary(final_mod)$adj.r.squared

# SPSS “ANOVA” table → R’s anova()
anova(final_mod)

# 4.3 Outliers / influence diagnostics (SPSS’s OUTS)
rstudent(final_mod)        # Studentized residuals
influence.measures(final_mod)

```{r functions}
  
wrap_kable_extra <- function(df_one_row, n = 8, caption = NULL){
  #' df_one_row: a data.frame with exactly one row
  #' n:          max number of columns per chunk
  #' caption:    base caption (will append “(cols x–y)” automatically)
  
  stopifnot(nrow(df_one_row) == 1)
  all_cols <- colnames(df_one_row)
  
  # split column indices into chunks of size n
  idxs <- split(seq_along(all_cols), ceiling(seq_along(all_cols)/n))
  
  for(i in seq_along(idxs)){
    cols_i <- all_cols[idxs[[i]]]
    subdf  <- df_one_row[, cols_i, drop = FALSE]
    cap_i  <- if (is.null(caption)) "" else
      sprintf("%s (cols %d–%d)", caption, min(idxs[[i]]), max(idxs[[i]]))
  
    subdf %>%
      kable(
        # preserve whatever format and options you were using
        format       = "latex",      # or "html"
        booktabs     = TRUE,
        caption      = cap_i,
        escape       = FALSE         # or TRUE, as you need
      ) %>%
      kable_styling(
        latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down"),
        full_width    = FALSE,
        font_size     = 6           # or whatever you prefer
      ) %>%
      print()
  }
}
```

 mod_olsr <- ols_step_backward_p(mod_one, prem = 0.05)

# 2) Extract the final lm() from that object
mod_ols <- mod_olsr$model

# 3a) View the full summary (coefficients, R², etc.)
summary(mod_ols)

.

When you run a pure backward‐elimination (either via base `step()` or `olsrr::ols_step_backward_p()`), any predictor whose p‐value exceeds your “POUT” threshold (.10 by SPSS’s default) will be dropped—even if SPSS happened to keep it (differences in the exact algorithm or data can lead to slightly different “last in/out” decisions).

---

### 1. Why MONTHS\_6TO22 and MONTHS\_23TO30 got dropped

* **Different p‐values:** In your R fit, once other covariates were removed or re‐estimated, those two had p > 0.10, so the routine removed them.
* **Algorithmic tweaks:** SPSS and R may handle tied p‐values, collinearities or ordering of removals slightly differently, so the “final” set can differ by one or two variables.

---

### 2. Forcing those variables to stay

You can tell R’s `step()` that your *minimal* model must always include those two.  Use the **`scope`** argument with a **lower** bound:

```r
# 1) Fit the full model like before
full_mod <- lm(
  LN_SPPSF ~ ARTERIAL
    + SINGLE_FAMILY1STORY + … + CRAWL + SLAB
    + LN_GARAGESPACES + FIREPLACE
    + HOT_WATER + CENTRAL_AIR
    + MONTHS_6TO22 + MONTHS_23TO30,
  data = df,
  na.action = na.omit
)

# 2) Define your “must‐keep” lower model
lower_mod <- lm(
  LN_SPPSF ~ MONTHS_6TO22 + MONTHS_23TO30,
  data = df, na.action = na.omit
)

# 3) Run backward with scope
forced_mod <- step(
  object    = full_mod,
  scope     = list(lower = formula(lower_mod),
                   upper = formula(full_mod)),
  direction = "backward",
  trace     = 1    # to see each variable dropped
)

# 4) Check that those months stayed in
summary(forced_mod)$coefficients
```

Because `step()` won’t remove anything below your **lower** bound, `MONTHS_6TO22` and `MONTHS_23TO30` will survive the elimination loop.

---

### 3. If you’re using **olsrr::ols\_step\_backward\_p()**

That function doesn’t directly support a “keep” list, so you have two choices:

1. **Use base `step()` with `scope`** (as above).
2. **After** your `ols_step_backward_p()` run, if those month variables aren’t in `step_mod$model`, you can re-fit the final model with them forced back in:

   ```r
   kept <- names(coef(step_mod$model))
   forced_final <- lm(
     reformulate(
       response = "LN_SPPSF",
       terms    = unique(c(kept, "MONTHS_6TO22", "MONTHS_23TO30"))
     ),
     data = df, na.action = na.omit
   )
   summary(forced_final)
   ```

---

**Bottom line:** backward routines will drop any variable that doesn’t meet your removal criterion. To *guarantee* `MONTHS_6TO22` and `MONTHS_23TO30` stay, either

* plug them into the **lower** formula of `step()`, or
* manually re-add them in a final re-fit.

.

predictors_A <- c("CRAWL","x2","x3")           # model A
predictors_B <- c("CRAWL","x2","x3","x4","x5") # model B (e.g., larger set)

# ---- build a shared split & folds (so models are compared fairly) ----
keep_all <- intersect(names(df), unique(c(target, predictors_A, predictors_B)))
stopifnot(target %in% keep_all)
df_base  <- df[, keep_all, drop = FALSE]
df_base  <- df_base[is.finite(df_base[[target]]), , drop = FALSE]

split  <- initial_split(df_base, prop = 0.8, strata = !!sym(target))
train  <- training(split)
test   <- testing(split)
folds  <- vfold_cv(train, v = 10, strata = !!sym(target))

# ---- helper: fit + assess one linear model on the shared split ----
assess_linear_on_split <- function(split, folds, predictors, normalize = TRUE) {
  tr <- training(split)
  te <- testing(split)

  # Drop everything except the chosen predictors + outcome inside the recipe
  drop_cols <- setdiff(names(tr), c(target, predictors))

  rec <- recipe(as.formula(paste(target, "~ .")), data = tr) %>%
    step_rm(all_of(drop_cols)) %>%
    step_naomit(all_predictors(), all_outcomes()) %>%
    step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    { if (normalize) step_normalize(., all_numeric_predictors()) else . }

  spec <- linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm")
  wf   <- workflow() %>% add_model(spec) %>% add_recipe(rec)

  # CV metrics
  cv_fit <- fit_resamples(
    wf, folds, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae, rsq),
    control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
  )

  # Train/Test metrics
  last   <- last_fit(wf, split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae, rsq))

  # Pull the trained lm() for diagnostics
  lm_fit <- extract_fit_parsnip(last$.workflow[[1]])$fit

  out <- list(
    wf      = wf,
    cv      = cv_fit,
    last    = last,
    lm_fit  = lm_fit,
    coef    = tidy(lm_fit, conf.int = TRUE),
    glance  = glance(lm_fit),                 # R^2, adj R^2, AIC, BIC, sigma, df, ...
    bp      = tryCatch(lmtest::bptest(lm_fit), error = function(e) NULL),
    shapiro = tryCatch(if (length(residuals(lm_fit)) <= 5000)
                         shapiro.test(residuals(lm_fit)) else NULL,
                       error = function(e) NULL),
    vif     = tryCatch({
                v <- car::vif(lm_fit)
                tibble(term = names(v), vif = as.numeric(v))
              }, error = function(e) NULL)
  )
  class(out) <- c("lm_assessment", class(out))
  out
}

res_A <- assess_linear_on_split(split, folds, predictors_A, normalize = TRUE)
res_B <- assess_linear_on_split(split, folds, predictors_B, normalize = TRUE)

# ---- pretty tables: CV means/SEs, test metrics, coefficients, diagnostics ----
tbl <- function(x, cap = NULL, digits = 4) {
  knitr::kable(x, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = digits, caption = cap) |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"))
}

# Cross-validated means
cv_A <- collect_metrics(res_A$cv) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Linear A")
cv_B <- collect_metrics(res_B$cv) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Linear B")
cv_compare <- dplyr::bind_rows(cv_A, cv_B) |>
  dplyr::select(model, .metric, mean, std_err) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = c(mean, std_err))
tbl(cv_compare, cap = "10-fold CV metrics (mean ± SE)")

# Test-set metrics
test_A <- collect_metrics(res_A$last) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Linear A")
test_B <- collect_metrics(res_B$last) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Linear B")
test_compare <- dplyr::bind_rows(test_A, test_B) |>
  dplyr::select(model, .metric, .estimate) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = .estimate)
tbl(test_compare, cap = "Hold-out test metrics")

# Coefficients (training fit inside last_fit)
tbl(res_A$coef, cap = "Linear A: coefficients (95% CI)")
tbl(res_B$coef, cap = "Linear B: coefficients (95% CI)")

# Model-level diagnostics
diag_A <- dplyr::tibble(
  stat = c("R^2", "Adj R^2", "AIC", "BIC", "Sigma",
           "Breusch–Pagan p", "Shapiro p (resid)"),
  value = c(res_A$glance$r.squared,
            res_A$glance$adj.r.squared,
            res_A$glance$AIC,
            res_A$glance$BIC,
            res_A$glance$sigma,
            if (!is.null(res_A$bp)) res_A$bp$p.value else NA_real_,
            if (!is.null(res_A$shapiro)) res_A$shapiro$p.value else NA_real_)
)
diag_B <- dplyr::tibble(
  stat = diag_A$stat,
  value = c(res_B$glance$r.squared,
            res_B$glance$adj.r.squared,
            res_B$glance$AIC,
            res_B$glance$BIC,
            res_B$glance$sigma,
            if (!is.null(res_B$bp)) res_B$bp$p.value else NA_real_,
            if (!is.null(res_B$shapiro)) res_B$shapiro$p.value else NA_real_)
)
tbl(dplyr::bind_cols(model = "Linear A", diag_A), cap = "Diagnostics: Linear A")
tbl(dplyr::bind_cols(model = "Linear B", diag_B), cap = "Diagnostics: Linear B")

if (!is.null(res_A$vif)) tbl(res_A$vif, cap = "Linear A: VIF")
if (!is.null(res_B$vif)) tbl(res_B$vif, cap = "Linear B: VIF")

# ---- paired per-fold comparison (A vs B on identical folds) ----
fold_A <- collect_metrics(res_A$cv, summarize = FALSE)
fold_B <- collect_metrics(res_B$cv, summarize = FALSE)

paired <- dplyr::left_join(
  fold_A, fold_B,
  by = c("id", ".metric", ".estimator"),
  suffix = c("_A", "_B")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(delta = .estimate_B - .estimate_A) |>
  dplyr::select(id, .metric, delta)

delta_summary <- paired |>
  dplyr::group_by(.metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_delta = mean(delta), sd_delta = sd(delta), .groups = "drop")
tbl(delta_summary, cap = "Per-fold mean delta (Linear B − Linear A)")

# Rough paired t-test on RMSE deltas (H0: mean delta = 0)
if (any(paired$.metric == "rmse")) {
  d_rmse <- paired$delta[paired$.metric == "rmse"]
  print(t.test(d_rmse, mu = 0))
}

# ---- nested-model F-test (if one predictor set is a strict subset of the other) ----
is_nested_AinB <- all(predictors_A %in% predictors_B)
is_nested_BinA <- all(predictors_B %in% predictors_A)
if (is_nested_AinB || is_nested_BinA) {
  # Compare training fits from the same split
  an <- if (is_nested_AinB) anova(res_A$lm_fit, res_B$lm_fit) else anova(res_B$lm_fit, res_A$lm_fit)
  print(an)
}

# ---- simple plots for the PDF (test set) ----
lmA_pred <- collect_predictions(res_A$last) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Linear A")
lmB_pred <- collect_predictions(res_B$last) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Linear B")
pred_both <- dplyr::bind_rows(lmA_pred, lmB_pred) |>
  dplyr::mutate(resid = !!sym(target) - .pred)

# Observed vs Predicted
ggplot(pred_both, aes(x = .pred, y = !!sym(target), color = model)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ model) +
  labs(title = "Hold-out: Predicted vs Observed", x = "Predicted", y = "Observed") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")

# Residuals vs Fitted
ggplot(pred_both, aes(x = .pred, y = resid, color = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ model) +
  labs(title = "Hold-out Residuals vs Fitted", x = "Fitted", y = "Residual") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")

nrmse_sd_vec <- function(truth, estimate) {
  sd_y <- stats::sd(truth, na.rm = TRUE)
  rmse <- yardstick::rmse_vec(truth, estimate)
  100 * (rmse / sd_y)
}

library(dplyr)
library(gt)
library(rlang)

gt_highlight_matches <- function(data,
                                 col_a, col_b,
                                 n = 10,
                                 highlight = "#fff3bf",
                                 na_matches = c("never", "both")) {
  na_matches <- match.arg(na_matches)
  ca <- ensym(col_a); cb <- ensym(col_b)

  d <- data %>%
    slice_head(n = n) %>%
    mutate(
      .match_row = if (na_matches == "both") {
        (is.na(!!ca) & is.na(!!cb)) | (!is.na(!!ca) & !is.na(!!cb) & (!!ca == !!cb))
      } else {
        !is.na(!!ca) & !is.na(!!cb) & (!!ca == !!cb)
      }
    )

  gt_tbl <- d %>%
    gt() %>%
    # highlight col_a cells where the row matches
    tab_style(
      style = list(cell_fill(color = highlight), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      locations = cells_body(columns = !!ca, rows = .match_row)
    ) %>%
    # highlight col_b cells where the row matches
    tab_style(
      style = list(cell_fill(color = highlight), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      locations = cells_body(columns = !!cb, rows = .match_row)
    ) %>%
    cols_hide(.match_row)

  gt_tbl
}

plot_lm_pvalues_two <- function(mod1, mod2, labels = c("Model 1", "Model 2"),
                                drop_intercept = TRUE, digits = 3, alpha_line = 0.05,
                                show_sidebar_labels = TRUE,
                                sidebar_space_mult = 0.35,  # how much right space to reserve
                                dodge_width = 0.5) { #labels next to dots: show_labels = TRUE
  acc <- 10^(-digits)
  eps <- 1e-16
  td1 <- broom::tidy(mod1) %>% mutate(.model = labels[1])
  td2 <- broom::tidy(mod2) %>% mutate(.model = labels[2])
  df <- bind_rows(td1, td2)

  if (drop_intercept) df <- df %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)")
  
  df <- df %>%    # clamp tiny p for log scale; build formatted label
    mutate(
      p_clamp   = pmax(p.value, eps),
      label_fmt = scales::number(p.value, accuracy = acc)
    )

  # order terms by the smallest p across models so rows are comparable
  order_df <- df %>%
    group_by(term) %>%
    summarise(p_min = min(p_clamp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  df <- df %>%
    left_join(order_df, by = "term") %>%
    mutate(term_ord = forcats::fct_reorder(term, p_min, .desc = TRUE)) # least sig at top
  
  pd <- position_dodge(dodge_width)    # dodge so two model points don’t overlap
  
  max_p <- max(df$p_clamp, na.rm = TRUE) # Where to place the sidebar labels (a fixed large x)
  label_x <- max_p * 10  # any factor > 1 works on log scale; we'll create space with expand

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = p_clamp, y = term_ord, colour = .model)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = pd) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = alpha_line, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    scale_x_log10(name = "P-Value (log scale)",
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, sidebar_space_mult))) +
    labs(
      title = "Predictor p-values by model", y = "Predictor", colour = "Model"
    ) + theme_minimal() + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + # allow text into the right margin
    theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 20, b = 5, l = 5, unit = "pt")) # bit of right margin

  if (show_sidebar_labels) {# Add 2 label columns (1 per model), positioned at a fixed large x
    lab_df <- df %>% mutate(x_for_label = label_x)

    p <- p +
      geom_text(data = lab_df,
                aes(x = x_for_label, y = term_ord, label = label_fmt, colour = .model),
                hjust = 0, size = 2.6, position = pd, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  p
}

plot_lm_pvalues_two_side <- function(mod1, mod2,
                                     labels = c("Model 1", "Model 2"),
                                     title = "Model",
                                     drop_intercept = TRUE,
                                     digits = 3,
                                     alpha_line = 0.05,
                                     show_sidebar_labels = TRUE,
                                     label_style = c("decimal","scientific"),
                                     format_axis_scientific = TRUE,   # tick labels
                                     dodge_width = 0.5,
                                     sidebar_hjust = -0.1,
                                     right_margin_pts = 90,
                                     legend_nudge_pts = 10) {

  label_style <- match.arg(label_style)
  acc <- 10^(-digits)
  eps <- 1e-16

  td1 <- broom::tidy(mod1) %>% mutate(.model = labels[1])
  td2 <- broom::tidy(mod2) %>% mutate(.model = labels[2])
  df  <- bind_rows(td1, td2)

  if (drop_intercept) df <- df %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)")

  # choose a label formatter
  lbl_fun <- if (label_style == "scientific") {
    scales::label_scientific(digits = digits)
  } else {
    function(x) scales::number(x, accuracy = acc)
  }

  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      p_clamp   = pmax(p.value, eps),
      label_fmt = lbl_fun(p.value)
    )

  # order rows by smallest p across models
  order_df <- df %>%
    group_by(term) %>%
    summarise(p_min = min(p_clamp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  df <- df %>%
    left_join(order_df, by = "term") %>%
    mutate(term_ord = forcats::fct_reorder(term, p_min, .desc = TRUE))

  pd <- position_dodge(width = dodge_width)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = p_clamp, y = term_ord, colour = .model)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = pd) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = alpha_line, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    scale_x_log10(
      name = "P-Value (log scale)",
      labels = if (format_axis_scientific) scales::label_scientific() else waiver()
    ) +
    labs(title = title, y = "Predictor", colour = "Model") +
    theme_minimal() +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = right_margin_pts, b = 5, l = 5, unit = "pt"),
      legend.box.margin = margin(l = legend_nudge_pts, unit = "pt")
    )

  if (show_sidebar_labels) {
    p <- p + geom_text(
      data = df,
      aes(x = Inf, y = term_ord, label = label_fmt, colour = .model),
      hjust = sidebar_hjust, size = 2.6, position = pd, inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
  }

  p
}

```{r mod_make_1, eval = FALSE}
full_model_A <- lm(LN_SPPSF ~ ARTERIAL + CRAWL + SLAB +    
                   SINGLE_FAMILY1STORY + SINGLE_FAMILY2STORY +
                   HALF_DUPLEX1STORY + HALF_DUPLEX2STORY +
                   SMALLEST + SMALL + LARGE + LARGEST + 
                   TWO_PLUS_BATHS + POWDER_ROOM + LN_GARAGESPACES + FIREPLACE +
                   GOOD + FAIR + POOR + VERY_POOR_UNSOUND + 
                   QABOVE_AVG + QBELOW_AVG + 
                   YB_PRE_1929 + YB_1930_TO_1945 + YB_1946_TO_1960 + YB_POST_1961 +
                   HOT_WATER + ELEC_BASEBOARD + WALL + CENTRAL_AIR +
                   MONTHS_1TO8 + MONTHS_9TO24,
                 data = A, na.action = na.omit)

f1A <- formula(full_model_A) 

# rows_use1A <- as.integer(rownames(model.frame(f1A, data = A, na.action = na.omit)))

mfA <- model.frame(full_model_A)       # already evaluated; no need to pass data
rows_use1A <- as.integer(rownames(mfA))
df_step1A  <- df[rows_use1A, , drop = FALSE]

full_locked1A <- lm(f1A, data = df_step1A, na.action = na.omit)

backward_model_1A <- stats::step(
  full_locked1A,
  direction = "backward",   
  trace = 0   
)

full_model_B <- lm(LN_SPPSF ~ ARTERIAL + CRAWL + SLAB +    # lm() is used to fit linear models
                   SINGLE_FAMILY1STORY + SINGLE_FAMILY2STORY +
                   HALF_DUPLEX1STORY + HALF_DUPLEX2STORY +
                   SMALLEST + SMALL + LARGE + LARGEST + #S_AVG +
                   TWO_PLUS_BATHS + POWDER_ROOM + LN_GARAGESPACES + FIREPLACE +
                   GOOD + FAIR + POOR + VERY_POOR_UNSOUND + #AVG + 
                   QABOVE_AVG + QBELOW_AVG + #Q_AVG +
                   YB_PRE_1929 + YB_1930_TO_1945 + YB_1946_TO_1960 + YB_POST_1961 +
                   HOT_WATER + ELEC_BASEBOARD + WALL + CENTRAL_AIR +
                   MONTHS_1TO8 + MONTHS_9TO24,
                 data = B, na.action = na.omit)

# 1) Take the exact formula from your full model
f1B <- formula(full_model_B) # formula() extracts formulae which have been included in other objects

# 2) Lock the row set to those complete for **all terms in f**
#rows_use1B <- as.integer(rownames(model.frame(f1B, data = B, na.action = na.omit)))
# as.integer() Creates or tests for objects of type "integer".
mfB <- model.frame(full_model_B)       # already evaluated; no need to pass data
rows_use1B <- as.integer(rownames(mfB))
df_step1B  <- df[rows_use1B, , drop = FALSE]

# (optional) sanity # length(rows_use)

# 3) Refit on the locked data, then step()
full_locked1B <- lm(f1B, data = df_step1B, na.action = na.omit)

backward_model_1B <- stats::step(
  # step() is IN the stats package, Selects a formula-based model by AIC
  full_locked1B,
  direction = "backward",    # direction indicates the mode of stepwise search
  trace = 0    # trace indicates verbose output
)
```
